**Short‑answer** > **Accept the contract only if you can secure a stop‑loss that protects against catastrophic episodes, carve‑outs (or an internal budget) for specialty/mental‑health/DME services, a realistic HEDIS bonus schedule, and a shared‑risk or risk‑corridor mechanism.** > If any of those safeguards are missing or negotiable only at the payer’s discretion, decline or renegotiate. --- ## 1. Why structure matters more than headline numbers | What matters | Why it matters | |--------------|----------------| | **Risk adjustment** | Medicare Advantage capitation is paid after CMS risk‑score adjustments (age, sex, comorbidity). A panel with many dual‑eligible or high‑cost patients can be under‑paid if the model is too blunt. | | **Stop‑loss / loss caps** | Full‑risk contracts expose you to unlimited losses on very expensive episodes (e.g., 90‑day post‑discharge readmissions). A per‑member stop‑loss (or a hard aggregate cap) protects cash flow. | | **Quality bonuses & penalties** | HEDIS bonuses add only $5–$15 PMPM in most MA contracts; penalties can wipe out that upside if thresholds are missed. The contract must spell out clear, transparent metrics and reporting. | | **Carve‑outs / specialty services** | If the payer expects you to deliver all care—including specialty, mental health, DME—your cost base will balloon. Separate carve‑out agreements keep those high‑cost, low‑volume services outside the capitation pool. | | **Shared‑risk or risk corridor** | A shared‑risk tier rewards efficient care and cushions you if utilization falls below a target. It also aligns incentives for quality improvement. | --- ## 2. Recommended deal structure (defensible across clinical, legal, and financial domains) | Component | Suggested terms | Rationale | |-----------|-----------------|-----------| | **Base capitation** | $1,180 PMPM (fixed) | Baseline revenue; reviewed annually against actual cost trends. | | **Risk adjustment** | CMS risk‑score payment + optional “dual‑eligible premium” of 2–3 % if the payer’s model under‑compensates for duals | Aligns payment with expected cost; keep it within CMS guidelines. | | **Stop‑loss / loss cap** | • Per‑member stop‑loss $15,000 (or $20,000)
• Aggregate loss cap $2–3 M (whichever is lower) | Protects against catastrophic episodes while being enforceable and realistic. | | **Carve‑outs** | Separate contracts for specialty care, mental health, and DME; payer pays 100 % of these services outside the capitation pool *if* the payer offers them; otherwise budget into capitation. | Keeps high‑cost, low‑volume services out of the risk equation. | | **Quality bonus** | Up to $10–$15 PMPM based on HEDIS thresholds (e.g., ≥90 % of benchmarks) + quarterly performance reports | Incentivizes preventive care; realistic for MA contracts. | | **Shared‑risk / risk corridor** | 10 % of the capitation pool as a risk corridor: if actual costs fall below the corridor, split savings 70/30 (group/payer). | Encourages efficient care coordination and aligns incentives. | | **Performance metrics** | Readmission ≤10 %, ED visit ≤15 %, preventive screening ≥90 % (per CMS standards) | Directly tied to bonus/penalty structure. | | **Data & reporting** | Secure data exchange agreements, de‑identified analytics, quarterly dashboards shared with payer | Enables real‑time risk monitoring and quality improvement. | | **Legal safeguards** | • Independent contracting language (no referral kickbacks).
• Compliance with Stark, Anti‑Kickback Statute, CMS Conditions of Participation.
• Audit rights for both parties.
• Balanced indemnification that protects the group from third‑party claims but does not absolve its own compliance responsibilities. | Reduces regulatory exposure and protects clinical autonomy. | | **Governance** | Joint steering committee (group physicians + payer reps) meeting quarterly to review metrics, adjust risk models, and resolve disputes. | Ensures alignment and rapid response to emerging issues. | --- ## 3. Clinical operations readiness 1. **Population‑health platform** – Integrate EHR data with analytics to generate real‑time risk scores, identify high‑cost patients, and trigger care‑management protocols. 2. **Case‑management team** – Dedicated staff (nurses, social workers) for dual‑eligible and complex chronic disease cohorts; must be paid at a rate that covers the higher cost of care. 3. **Preventive‑care workflow** – Automated reminders for screenings, vaccinations, and medication reconciliation to hit HEDIS targets. 4. **Telehealth & virtual visits** – Reduce ED utilization and readmissions; must be reimbursed under the capitation model. 5. **Care‑coordination protocols** – Standardized discharge plans, post‑acute care agreements, and 24/7 nurse lines to prevent costly readmissions. --- ## 4. Legal exposure mitigation | Risk | Mitigation | |------|------------| | **Anti‑kickback / Stark violations** | Explicitly state that no referrals or financial incentives are tied to patient choice of specialty services; carve‑outs keep specialty care separate. | | **CMS Conditions of Participation (CoP)** | Maintain independent clinical decision‑making; ensure all quality metrics are met and documented. | | **Patient privacy (HIPAA)** | Secure data exchange agreements, encryption, audit trails for analytics; use de‑identified data where possible to avoid unnecessary patient consent. | | **Contractual disputes** | Include a dispute‑resolution clause (mediation → arbitration) and clear definitions of “loss” and “stop‑loss.” | --- ## 5. Financial viability analysis (conservative baseline) | Item | PMPM | Annualized (25 k members) | |------|------|---------------------------| | **Base capitation** | $1,180 | $354 M | | **Estimated cost per member** | $750–$900 | $225–$270 M | | **Quality bonus (average 50 % of max)** | $7.5–$10 | $22–$30 M | | **Stop‑loss impact (worst case)** | –$1.5 | –$45 M | | **Net operating margin** | $300–$350 | $90–$105 M | *Key take‑away:* Even with a conservative cost estimate of $900 PMPM and a realistic quality bonus of $10 PMPM, the contract yields a gross margin of roughly 30–35 %. The stop‑loss protects against catastrophic loss events, keeping net margin above 20 %. --- ## 6. Implementation checklist | Step | Owner | Deadline | |------|-------|----------| | Finalize risk‑adjustment model & baseline cost audit | Finance/Analytics | Week 4 | | Negotiate stop‑loss and carve‑out clauses | Legal/Finance | Week 8 | | Build data‑exchange infrastructure (API, dashboards) | IT | Week 12 | | Train clinical staff on new workflows & quality metrics | Clinical Ops | Week 16 | | Sign joint steering committee charter | Group Leadership / Payer | Week 20 | | Conduct pre‑contract simulation run | Analytics | Week 24 | | Go‑live with contract | All | Month 7 | --- ## 7. Bottom line recommendation 1. **Accept the contract only if you can secure**: * A per‑member stop‑loss of $15–$20 k (or a realistic aggregate loss cap). * Separate carve‑out agreements for specialty/mental‑health/DME services, or an internal budget that reflects those costs. * A clear HEDIS bonus schedule ($5–$15 PMPM) with transparent reporting and penalty clauses. * A shared‑risk or risk‑corridor mechanism (10 % of the capitation pool). 2. **If any of those elements are missing, negotiable only at the payer’s discretion, or unrealistic** (e.g., $200 PMPM bonus, 20 % stop‑loss on total capitation), decline or renegotiate. With the above structure, your 40‑physician group can safely manage a 25 k Medicare Advantage panel, maintain high quality standards, and generate a defensible profit margin.
